name: Nigerian Tea
whatMakesItGood: What most people actually mean by tea: chocolate malt, powdered milk and enough sugar to start a morning.
description: Milo or Bournvita, hot water, milk. The drink that goes with bread.

steps.heading: Boil the water
steps.description: Bring a kettle to the boil and let it sit thirty seconds off the heat.

steps.heading: Build the cup
steps.description: Milo at the bottom, then milk powder, then sugar if you take it.

steps.heading: Pour and stir
steps.description: Pour slowly while stirring so the milk does not clump.

name: Bournvita and Milk
whatMakesItGood: Darker and less sweet than Milo on its own. The cocoa comes through properly.
description: Bournvita made the way it is actually drunk at home.

steps.heading: Boil the water
steps.description: A full kettle, then off the heat for a moment.

steps.heading: Dissolve
steps.description: Bournvita first with a splash of hot water, worked into a smooth paste.

steps.heading: Finish
steps.description: Top up with water and stir the evaporated milk through.

name: Black Tea
whatMakesItGood: Five minutes and nothing to clean. The brew is the whole decision.
description: Plain black tea, taken with milk and sugar or neither.

steps.heading: Boil
steps.description: Fresh water, fully boiling. Reboiled water makes tea taste flat.

steps.heading: Steep
steps.description: Three minutes for ordinary strength, five if you want it dark.

steps.heading: Finish
steps.description: Milk and sugar to taste, or leave it plain.

name: Ginger Tea
whatMakesItGood: Fresh ginger rather than a sachet, so it actually bites. Good on a cold morning or a blocked nose.
description: Ginger simmered with lemon and sweetened with honey.

steps.heading: Prepare the ginger
steps.description: Peel and slice thinly. More surface, more flavour.

steps.heading: Simmer
steps.description: Ten minutes in gently boiling water, lid on.

steps.heading: Finish
steps.description: Strain, squeeze in the lemon and stir honey in off the heat.

name: Green Tea with Lemon
whatMakesItGood: Water just off the boil, never fully boiling. Green tea turns bitter if you scald it.
description: A lighter morning cup for anyone skipping the sugar.

steps.heading: Heat the water
steps.description: Boil, then wait a full minute before pouring.

steps.heading: Steep briefly
steps.description: Two minutes only. Longer and it goes bitter.

name: Black Coffee
whatMakesItGood: Nothing hiding behind milk, so the water temperature matters.
description: Instant or ground, taken black.

steps.heading: Boil and rest
steps.description: Off the boil for thirty seconds so it does not scorch.

steps.heading: Pour
steps.description: Over the coffee, stir once, sugar if you take it.

name: Coffee with Milk
whatMakesItGood: Evaporated milk rather than fresh. It is thicker, and it is what most kitchens have.
description: Milky coffee, the everyday version.

steps.heading: Make the coffee
steps.description: Strong, in half a cup of hot water.

steps.heading: Warm the milk
steps.description: Briefly, so it does not cool the cup.

steps.heading: Combine
steps.description: Pour the milk in slowly and stir.

name: Pap and Milk
whatMakesItGood: The texture is everything. Boiling water poured fast and stirred hard is what makes it smooth.
description: Ogi, akamu, koko. Fermented corn pap with evaporated milk.

steps.heading: Slake the pap
steps.description: Mix with a little cold water until completely lump free.

steps.heading: Pour boiling water
steps.description: Fast, from a height, stirring hard the whole time until it thickens and turns glossy.

steps.heading: Finish
steps.description: Sugar and milk stirred through while hot.

name: Pap and Akara
whatMakesItGood: The classic pairing. Hot pap against crisp bean cakes is the point.
description: Akara fried fresh and eaten with smooth pap.

steps.heading: Season the paste
steps.description: Whisk the bean paste with chopped onion, pepper and salt until light and airy.

steps.heading: Heat the oil
steps.description: Deep and properly hot. Cool oil makes akara greasy.

steps.heading: Fry
steps.description: Spoon in and fry until deep gold on both sides. Drain well.

steps.heading: Make the pap
steps.description: Slake, pour boiling water and stir until smooth.

name: Quick Instant Pap
whatMakesItGood: Five minutes when there is no time to stand over a pot.
description: Instant pap, hot water, milk.

steps.heading: Mix dry
steps.description: Pap, milk powder and sugar together in the bowl first.

steps.heading: Add water
steps.description: Boiling water, poured while stirring, until it thickens.

name: Oats and Milk
whatMakesItGood: Cooked in milk rather than water, which is the difference between breakfast and wallpaper paste.
description: Oats simmered with milk, sweetened lightly.

steps.heading: Simmer
steps.description: Oats and milk on low, stirring now and then.

steps.heading: Season
steps.description: A pinch of salt lifts it. Sugar to taste.

steps.heading: Rest
steps.description: Two minutes off the heat to thicken properly.

name: Banana Oats
whatMakesItGood: Mash half the banana into the pot and it sweetens the whole thing without sugar.
description: Oats with banana, groundnut and honey.

steps.heading: Cook the oats
steps.description: In milk, low heat, until thick.

steps.heading: Mash one banana
steps.description: Stir it through the pot so it sweetens everything.

steps.heading: Top
steps.description: Slice the second banana over, with groundnut and honey.

name: Cornflakes and Milk
whatMakesItGood: No cooking at all. Honest about what it is.
description: Cornflakes, cold milk, done.

steps.heading: Mix the milk
steps.description: Powdered milk into cold water until smooth, or use it straight from a carton.

steps.heading: Pour
steps.description: Over the flakes, and eat before they go soft.

name: Custard and Milk
whatMakesItGood: Same technique as pap, different flavour. Boiling water and a hard stir.
description: Custard powder made thick, with milk.

steps.heading: Make a paste
steps.description: Custard powder with a little cold water, no lumps.

steps.heading: Pour boiling water
steps.description: Stirring hard until it thickens and the colour deepens.

steps.heading: Finish
steps.description: Milk and sugar stirred in.

name: Pap and Moin Moin
whatMakesItGood: Steamed bean pudding instead of fried. Lighter than akara and it keeps better.
description: Moin moin steamed and served with smooth pap.

steps.heading: Season the paste
steps.description: Blend in onion, palm oil and salt until loose enough to pour.

steps.heading: Fill
steps.description: Into bowls or wraps. Add egg if you are using it.

steps.heading: Steam
steps.description: Forty minutes, covered, until a knife comes out clean.

steps.heading: Make the pap
steps.description: While it steams.

name: Bread and Egg Sauce
whatMakesItGood: The sauce does the work. Eggs go in last and stay soft, so the bread has something to soak up.
description: Agege bread with a proper tomato and egg sauce.

steps.heading: Start the sauce
steps.description: Fry diced tomato and onion until the raw smell goes and the oil separates.

steps.heading: Season
steps.description: Dry pepper and salt. Cook it down until thick, not watery.

steps.heading: Fold in the eggs
steps.description: Beaten, poured in, stirred slowly and off the heat while still glossy.

steps.heading: Serve
steps.description: Tear the bread rather than slicing it.

name: Fried Egg Sandwich
whatMakesItGood: Ten minutes from nothing to a full meal, and the yolk is the sauce.
description: Toasted bread, fried eggs, raw onion.

steps.heading: Toast
steps.description: Butter one side of each slice and toast face down in a dry pan.

steps.heading: Fry the eggs
steps.description: Soft yolk is the point, so pull them early.

steps.heading: Build
steps.description: Eggs, raw onion, close it and press once.

name: Bread and Egg Toast
whatMakesItGood: Bread soaked in seasoned egg and fried. Nothing extra, and it still tastes like an effort.
description: French toast, the way it is made here.

steps.heading: Make the dip
steps.description: Eggs beaten with milk, salt and sugar until smooth.

steps.heading: Soak briefly
steps.description: A few seconds each side only, or the middle collapses.

steps.heading: Fry
steps.description: Medium heat until both sides are gold and the centre is set.

name: Egg and Sardine Bread
whatMakesItGood: Sardine and egg together make it a meal instead of a snack. Store cupboard, start to finish.
description: Flaked sardine scrambled through egg, in bread.

steps.heading: Fry the base
steps.description: Onion and chilli in oil, keeping some bite.

steps.heading: Add the sardine
steps.description: Drained and flaked, oil and all. Break it up, do not mash it.

steps.heading: Scramble
steps.description: Beaten eggs folded through until just set. Taste before salting.

steps.heading: Serve
steps.description: Into split bread while hot.

name: Egg and Sausage Bread
whatMakesItGood: Sausage renders its own fat and the egg cooks in it, so nothing tastes dry.
description: Sausage, pepper and egg in buttered bread.

steps.heading: Brown the sausage
steps.description: Sliced into coins, fried until the edges catch. Keep the fat.

steps.heading: Add vegetables
steps.description: Bell pepper and the white of the spring onion, into the fat.

steps.heading: Set the eggs
steps.description: Poured over, stirred until just cooked. Green tops last.

steps.heading: Fill
steps.description: Butter the bread and fill generously.

name: Bread, Egg and Fried Plantain
whatMakesItGood: Sweet plantain against peppery egg. The plate that turns breakfast into something you sit down for.
description: Fried plantain, egg sauce and agege bread.

steps.heading: Fry the plantain
steps.description: Thick rounds, lightly salted, until the edges go dark gold. Drain.

steps.heading: Pour off the oil
steps.description: Keep two spoons. Save the rest.

steps.heading: Build the egg sauce
steps.description: Onion and tomato with pepper until thick, then fold in beaten eggs.

steps.heading: Plate
steps.description: Bread one side, plantain the other, egg in the middle.

name: Boiled Egg and Bread
whatMakesItGood: The simplest thing on this list. Timing the egg is the only skill involved.
description: Soft-boiled eggs, buttered bread, salt and pepper.

steps.heading: Boil
steps.description: Seven minutes from boiling for a set white and a soft yolk.

steps.heading: Cool
steps.description: Straight into cold water so they peel cleanly.

steps.heading: Serve
steps.description: Buttered bread, egg sliced over, salt and pepper.

name: Boiled Yam and Egg Sauce
whatMakesItGood: Yam needs salt in the water, not after. That is the whole trick.
description: Boiled yam with a peppery egg sauce.

steps.heading: Boil the yam
steps.description: Peeled, cut into rounds, salted water, until a knife slides through.

steps.heading: Fry the sauce
steps.description: Tomato and onion in palm oil until thick and the oil clears.

steps.heading: Add the eggs
steps.description: Beaten, folded through, taken off while soft.

name: Fried Yam and Pepper Sauce
whatMakesItGood: Dry the yam before it hits the oil or it will never crisp.
description: Yam chips with ata din din.

steps.heading: Cut and salt
steps.description: Batons, rinsed, then patted completely dry.

steps.heading: Fry
steps.description: Hot oil, in batches, until gold and crisp at the edges.

steps.heading: Drain and serve
steps.description: On paper, salted while hot, with the pepper sauce.

name: Fried Plantain and Eggs
whatMakesItGood: Ripe plantain only. Anything less and it fries without sweetening.
description: Dodo with scrambled eggs.

steps.heading: Fry the dodo
steps.description: Diced or sliced, until the edges caramelise.

steps.heading: Scramble
steps.description: In a spoon of the same oil with onion, soft and just set.

steps.heading: Serve
steps.description: Together, hot.

name: Light Yam Porridge
whatMakesItGood: A breakfast version: less oil, more water, so it stays light.
description: Yam cooked soft in a thin palm oil broth.

steps.heading: Boil the yam
steps.description: Cubed, in just enough water to cover.

steps.heading: Season
steps.description: Palm oil, onion, pepper and crayfish in while it cooks.

steps.heading: Mash lightly
steps.description: Crush some of the yam against the pot to thicken the liquid.

name: Boiled Sweet Potato and Egg
whatMakesItGood: Sweeter than yam and it cooks faster, so watch it.
description: Sweet potato boiled, with egg sauce.

steps.heading: Boil
steps.description: Peeled and cut, in salted water, until just tender.

steps.heading: Make the sauce
steps.description: Tomato and onion fried down, eggs folded in.

steps.heading: Serve
steps.description: Together, while both are hot.

name: Akara and Bread
whatMakesItGood: Hot akara inside soft bread. Eaten standing up on the way out of the house.
description: Bean cakes in agege bread.

steps.heading: Season
steps.description: Whisk the paste with onion, pepper and salt until airy.

steps.heading: Fry
steps.description: Properly hot oil, until deep gold. Drain.

steps.heading: Fill
steps.description: Split the bread and pack it in.

name: Soaked Garri and Groundnut
whatMakesItGood: No fire at all. Cold water, garri, groundnut, sugar.
description: Garri soaked and eaten with roasted groundnut.

steps.heading: Soak
steps.description: Garri into cold water and let it swell for two minutes.

steps.heading: Top
steps.description: Groundnut, sugar and milk over the top.

name: Morning Fruit Bowl
whatMakesItGood: Cut it the moment you eat it. Fruit sitting in a bowl loses everything.
description: Pawpaw, pineapple, watermelon and banana.

steps.heading: Prepare
steps.description: Peel and cube everything to roughly the same size.

steps.heading: Dress
steps.description: A squeeze of lemon stops the banana browning and lifts the rest.

name: Yoghurt with Fruit and Groundnut
whatMakesItGood: Assembly, not cooking. The groundnut is what stops it feeling like a snack.
description: Yoghurt layered with fruit, groundnut and honey.

steps.heading: Layer
steps.description: Yoghurt, then sliced banana, then oats if using.

steps.heading: Finish
steps.description: Groundnut over the top and honey across it.

name: Indomie and Egg
whatMakesItGood: Two minutes of noodles and an egg folded in. Nobody is pretending otherwise.
description: Noodles with egg, onion and pepper.

steps.heading: Boil the noodles
steps.description: Three minutes, then drain almost all the water.

steps.heading: Fry the base
steps.description: Onion and chilli in oil until soft.

steps.heading: Combine
steps.description: Noodles in with the seasoning, then the beaten egg folded through.

name: Tiger Nut Milk
whatMakesItGood: Blended and strained properly, it is thick enough to drink on its own.
description: Kunu aya, blended fresh with dates.

steps.heading: Soak
steps.description: Overnight if you can, or an hour in warm water.

steps.heading: Blend
steps.description: With dates, coconut and ginger, and plenty of water.

steps.heading: Strain
steps.description: Through a clean cloth, pressing hard. Chill before drinking.
